This script builds the map layers every study shares: states with their UNOS region, region outlines, region numbers, adult heart-transplant centers and the extent of the corridor inset.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/map_geography.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/UNOS-mapping/blob/main/R/map_geography.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/UNOS-mapping/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/UNOS-mapping/blob/main/R/functions.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/map_geography.R")
```

## States and regions

In the original scripts this took three files: a spreadsheet listing each region's states, the 2018 Census state shapefile, and code to split, pivot and join them. sRtr was built from exactly that code, so the result now ships with the package as `UNOS_regions_sf`: one row per state (the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia) with its region. `get_hrsa_optn_regions()` dissolves the states into one outline per region. Both are put in `map_crs`, so every layer shares one projection.

```{r}
#| label: region-geography
#| eval: false
```

## Transplant centers

The original maps used a copy of an HRSA transplant-center file downloaded once. `get_hrsa_transplant_centers()` downloads the current layer from HRSA each time it runs [@hrsa_otc_layer], which is then narrowed to adult heart centers (see [Functions](functions.qmd#choosing-the-transplant-centers)).

The layer shows centers as they are on the day the code runs, not as they were during each study period, so a center that has since opened or closed may be shown wrongly. That is accepted here because the maps teach the method ([plan §4](analysis-plan.qmd#4-data-sources-and-measurement-periods)). The download date is recorded, and goes into the note printed under every map, so a figure that leaves this site still says which list its dots come from and that they are not the study period's centers.

```{r}
#| label: heart-centers
#| eval: false
```

## The corridor inset

The inset enlarges the Washington-Boston corridor, the stretch from DC through Baltimore, Philadelphia, New York and Hartford to Providence and Boston where centers crowd together. The extent is set in longitude and latitude in `R/setup.R`, which is easier to read and change than projected coordinates. Here it is turned into a box in `map_crs`. Projecting a rectangle bends its edges, so the box is projected as a polygon and its bounding box taken, so that no corner of the corridor is cut off. The box is kept as a polygon, `corridor_box`, because the tmap maps draw it in red on the main map and use it to place the region numbers.

```{r}
#| label: corridor-inset
#| eval: false
```

## Region numbers

Each region's number sits on a point from `st_point_on_surface()`, which is guaranteed to fall inside the region; a centroid can fall outside a region whose shape is irregular. These points replace the hand-entered label positions the original maps read from a spreadsheet.

The corridor inset needs two sets of points, made by `place_region_labels()` (see [Functions](functions.qmd#placing-the-region-numbers)). `main_labels` keeps every number clear of the red box on the main map. `inset_labels` gives every region that appears in the enlarged view its own number there: Regions 1, 2, 9 and 11.

```{r}
#| label: region-labels
#| eval: false
```
